script.title: Kodak’s Camera That Used a Cassette
script.hook_line: Kodak’s first digital camera saved pictures on a cassette tape.
script.close_line: At Eastman Kodak in nineteen seventy-five, Steve Sasson invented the first digital camera. His prototype needed twenty-three seconds to write a single image to cassette. segments.say: Kodak’s first digital camera saved pictures on a cassette tape.
In nineteen seventy-four, Gareth Lloyd asked Steve Sasson to see if a new device that captured light could serve as a camera’s image sensor.
The sensor could capture an image but couldn’t store it, so Sasson built a camera that held the image in memory before transferring it to tape.
In nineteen seventy-five, Sasson took his first picture with the camera.
The pictures were grainy and black and white, and the cassette drive that recorded them was part of the camera itself.
Sasson built a playback system too, and his plan was to take people’s pictures in the conference room and show them right there on a television.
But even after a few demonstrations, Kodak executives said they didn’t see a market for the camera.
In nineteen eighty-nine, Sasson and Robert Hills developed a digital single-lens reflex camera, but Kodak initially declined to sell it to protect its film sales.
In nineteen ninety-four, Sasson worked with Nikon to build one of the first digital cameras people could buy.
In May of two thousand, Kodak first made Sasson’s prototype camera known to the public during a presentation on the evolution of digital cameras.
segments.say_first: In two thousand, Kodak publicly revealed the cassette prototype in a presentation about how digital cameras had evolved.

segments.say: The camera that took twenty-three seconds to record a picture on tape earned Sasson the two thousand nine National Medal of Technology and Innovation.

spine.claim: Steve Sasson invented the first digital camera at Eastman Kodak in 1975.

source.quote: Sasson invented the first digital camera in 1975 while working at Eastman Kodak, in Rochester, N.Y.

spine.claim: Sasson's prototype recorded images on a cassette tape in 23 seconds per image.

source.quote: The images were digitally recorded onto a cassette tape, a process that took twenty-three seconds per image.

spine.claim: Kodak initially declined to sell the digital SLR Sasson helped develop because it wanted to protect film sales.

source.quote: To protect the company’s film sales, Kodak initially declined to sell the product.

spine.claim: Steve Sasson was awarded the 2009 National Medal of Technology and Innovation.

source.quote: Sasson was awarded the 2009 National Medal of Technology and Innovation.

spine.claim: Sasson received a patent for his original camera, which never went into production.

source.quote: Sasson fixed those problems and was granted a U.S. patent for the camera in 1978, but it was never put into production.
